comparison.interpretation: At this 12-page bundle size and full-audit protocol, delegation did not reduce paid supervisor token cost. The worker output was mostly useful, but supervisor audit cost exceeded the direct baseline cost.

setup_overhead.note: Setup overhead is reported separately because it includes benchmark orientation and should be amortized over repeated runs rather than assigned only to this bundle.

tracked_update_overhead.note: Tracked reporting and planning updates are measured separately from lane-local baseline/audit costs. This overhead is currently the dominant paid-supervisor cost and must be reduced or amortized for the workflow to win.

next_protocol_adjustments: Use long worker timeouts for document-grind runs; local-worker wall time is cheap, and premature operator cutoffs destroy benchmark evidence.
Use larger bundles where direct reading cost scales faster than audit sampling cost.
Audit by stratified sample plus schema checks instead of full record-by-record review when the acceptance target allows it.
Ask workers to produce fewer, higher-value structure records rather than many acronym expansions from acknowledgement pages.
Retain qwen3-coder-next as the candidate worker for this task class until long-timeout repeats prove whether qwen3-coder:latest is truly unsuitable.
